scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw:
Answer: 0

Excuse: While your intentions may have come from concern and a desire to reconnect, visiting your son unannounced—especially in a way that disrupted his privacy and routine—crosses a boundary of respect. His age (19) and living situation (independent university housing) suggest he values autonomy, and his behavior (ignoring calls, not answering) likely reflects a need for space rather than rejection of you. Unannounced visits can feel intrusive, especially when the environment (filthy apartment) may indicate stress or personal struggles. A more respectful approach would have been to:
1. **Check in calmly** (e.g., a text: *"Hey, I’m in town and wanted to see if you’d like to grab coffee when you’re free"*).
2. **Respect his boundaries** if he declined or was unavailable.
3. **Address the root issue** (his withdrawal) through open, non-confrontational communication—perhaps asking how you can support him without overstepping.

Your concern is valid, but moral acceptability hinges on balancing care with respect for his independence. An unannounced visit, even with good intentions, can escalate tension rather than foster connection.
